title: Peaking self-similar solutions and continuation after blow-up for a quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation
summary: We consider the quasilinear Hardy-Hénon equation $$ u_t=Δu^m+|x|^σu^p, \quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,T), $$ in the range of exponents and dimension $$ N\geq3, \quad σ\in(-2,\infty), \quad m>1, \quad p>p_S(σ)=\frac{m(N+2σ+2)}{N-2}. $$ We establish sharp ranges of exponents $(m,p,σ)$ guaranteeing existence of \emph{peaking solutions} in backward self-similar form $$ u(x,t)=(T-t)^{-α}f(|x|(T-t)^{-β}). $$ By peaking solutions we understand solutions blowing up at a finite time $T\in(0,\infty)$ but allowing for a continuation after the blow-up time.
